panSubstrates.name: Bare Unlined Copper (C11000 Pure ETP Copper)
panSubstrates.acidReactivityIndex: Extreme (Rapid dissolution of Cu2+ ions in pH < 6.0)
panSubstrates.fdaCompliance: Violates FDA Food Code Sec 4-101.14 for acidic foods (pH < 6.0)
panSubstrates.description: Solid electrolytic tough-pitch copper without any protective barrier. Boasts the highest thermal responsiveness of any cookware metal (k = 401 W/m·K), but exhibits extreme chemical reactivity toward organic food acids. When exposed to acids, oxygen, and heat, copper ionizes rapidly into soluble Cu2+ cations and toxic verdigris salts, imparting a harsh metallic penny taste and precipitating acute nausea.

panSubstrates.name: Pristine Hand-Wiped Tin-Lined Copper (100% Intact Tin)
panSubstrates.acidReactivityIndex: Inert (Pure food-grade tin resists organic acids up to pH 2.0)
panSubstrates.fdaCompliance: Fully Compliant with FDA Food Code (hermetic tin barrier)
panSubstrates.description: Heavy copper pan lined with a hand-wiped layer of 99.7%+ pure culinary tin applied via molten fluxing at 235°C. Pure tin is completely non-reactive to tomato, wine, and citrus acids. However, tin possesses a low melting point (231.9°C / 449°F) and a soft Mohs hardness of 1.5, making it susceptible to accidental melting if dry-preheated or abrasive scratching if scrubbed with steel wool.

panSubstrates.name: Worn Tin-Lined Copper (>25mm / US Quarter-Size Bare Spot)
panSubstrates.acidReactivityIndex: High (Galvanic corrosion accelerates bare copper dissolution)
panSubstrates.description: A vintage or heavily used copper pot where abrasive scouring or metal utensils have stripped the tin lining, exposing bare copper patches exceeding a US 25-cent coin (24.3 mm diameter / ~4.6 cm²). The electrical contact between tin and copper creates a galvanic corrosion cell in the presence of acidic liquid electrolytes, accelerating copper leaching into the simmering food.

panSubstrates.name: Stainless Steel-Clad Copper Bimetal (18/10 AISI 304)
panSubstrates.acidReactivityIndex: Zero (Chromium-oxide passivation layer completely impervious to acid)
panSubstrates.fdaCompliance: Fully Compliant with FDA Food Code across all food matrices
panSubstrates.description: Modern multi-layer cookware featuring a 2.3mm heavy copper outer shell diffusion-bonded or high-pressure roll-cladded to an internal 0.2mm liner of austenitic 18/10 stainless steel (AISI 304). Combines lightning-fast copper heat distribution with the bulletproof, non-reactive, acid-proof properties of passive chromium oxide (Cr2O3). Never needs re-tinning and permits high-temperature searing.

panSubstrates.name: Vintage Nickel-Plated Copper (Mid-20th Century European)
panSubstrates.acidReactivityIndex: Moderate-High (Acid pitting leaches both nickel and substrate copper)
panSubstrates.fdaCompliance: Restricted (High nickel leaching risk for sensitized individuals)
panSubstrates.description: Commonly produced in mid-20th century France and Germany as a harder, higher-melting alternative to tin. While resistant to melting up to 1455°C, acidic foods (especially vinegar and tomato) induce micro-pitting in thin electroplated nickel layers. This causes significant nickel leaching (a major allergen triggering systemic contact dermatitis) followed by rapid exposure and dissolution of the underlying copper.

panSubstrates.name: Cast Brass / Bronze Cookware & Handles (Cu-Zn Alloy)
panSubstrates.acidReactivityIndex: High (Dezincification and leaching of copper and potential trace lead)
panSubstrates.fdaCompliance: Prohibited for acidic food contact under FDA Food Code Sec 4-101.14
panSubstrates.description: Culinary vessels and handles cast from alpha-beta brass (60-70% copper, 30-40% zinc) or decorative bronze. Acidic foods trigger dezincification (selective leaching of zinc) and massive dissolution of copper. Furthermore, vintage and artisanal brass castings frequently contain 1–3% lead added to improve molten alloy fluidity, presenting a severe heavy metal neurotoxicity risk if used for food.

foodMatrices.name: Slow-Simmered Tomato Marinara / Bolognese
foodMatrices.organolepticEffect: Bitter metallic penny taste; sauce develops a dull muddy greenish-brown tinge as copper binds with lycopene
foodMatrices.description: The quintessential culinary risk scenario. The combination of aqueous citric and malic acids at 90°C accelerates the dissolution of copper metal into soluble cupric citrate and malate complexes. Simmering for more than 30 minutes in unlined or worn copper can produce over 20 mg/kg of dissolved copper, exceeding acute vomiting thresholds.

foodMatrices.name: Red Wine Pan Reduction (Coq au Vin / Bordelaise)
foodMatrices.category: High Acid, Tartaric Acid & Alcohol Solvent
foodMatrices.organolepticEffect: Sharp astringent metallic bitterness; wine anthocyanin pigments precipitate into an unappealing dark greyish sediment
foodMatrices.description: Ethanol acts as an organic co-solvent while tartaric acid acts as an aggressive bidentate chelating ligand for copper ions. Copper ions catalyze rapid oxidation of wine polyphenols, destroying delicate aromatic esters and creating an intensely unpleasant acrid, puckering metallic aftertaste.

foodMatrices.name: Lemon Curd & Citrus Beurre Blanc
foodMatrices.organolepticEffect: Instant bright emerald-green discoloration; acute burning chemical taste that ruins delicate egg and butter emulsions
foodMatrices.description: With a high concentration of free hydronium ions (pH 2.3), citrus juice attacks bare copper instantaneously. Ascorbic acid reduces copper to cuprous (Cu+) which then re-oxidizes, generating destructive hydroxyl radicals that break down emulsifiers while dissolving massive quantities of ionic copper.

foodMatrices.name: Balsamic Vinegar & Cider Pan Deglaze
foodMatrices.organolepticEffect: Forms soluble copper(II) acetate complexes; pungent metallic stench and severe throat irritation
foodMatrices.description: Hot aqueous acetic acid reacts directly with oxidized copper to synthesize copper(II) acetate monohydrate [Cu(CH3COO)2·H2O]—the primary chemical component of synthetic verdigris. Even a brief 3-minute reduction in a worn copper pan leaches heavy copper salt concentrations.

foodMatrices.name: Fruit Preserves & High-Sugar Jam (Confectionery Basin)
foodMatrices.category: Moderate Acid but High Sugar / Low Water Activity
foodMatrices.organolepticEffect: None when prepared traditionally; high sucrose binds free water molecules, inhibiting ionic copper diffusion
foodMatrices.description: Traditional French unlined copper jam pans (bassines à confiture) have been safely used for centuries. High sucrose concentrations (>65% dissolved sugars) drastically lower free water activity (Aw < 0.85), severely restricting the mobility of hydronium ions and limiting copper dissolution during rapid boiling, provided the jam is removed immediately after cooking.

foodMatrices.name: Whipped Egg Whites for Soufflés & Meringues
foodMatrices.organolepticEffect: Desirable creamy pale-gold hue; creates remarkably dense, stable foam that resists overwhipping and weeping
foodMatrices.description: The celebrated culinary chemistry exception discovered by French pastry chefs and verified by food scientists. In an alkaline unlined copper bowl, minute traces of copper ions (~1–2 ppm) detach and chelate with ovotransferrin (conalbumin) protein molecules. This forms a yellow copper-conalbumin complex that reinforces protein crosslinks, preventing denaturation from overbeating without any toxicity risk.

foodMatrices.name: Whole Milk & Pastry Cream Base
foodMatrices.organolepticEffect: None under normal conditions; neutral pH prevents significant copper dissolution
foodMatrices.description: Near-neutral pH (6.6–6.8) and milk proteins form a protective micellar buffer around the copper interface. Copper migration remains below 0.3 mg/kg, well within human nutritional tolerances, though sulfur compounds in milk can gradually tarnish the pan with brown copper sulfide.

verdigrisStates.name: Pristine Bright Polished Copper
verdigrisStates.visualDescription: Bright salmon-pink to reddish-gold metallic luster; zero visible tarnish or oxide films
verdigrisStates.solubilityInAcid: Moderate (Requires dissolved oxygen to initiate surface oxidation)
verdigrisStates.toxicityHazard: Baseline (Depends strictly on food acidity and cooking duration)

verdigrisStates.name: Brown Cuprous Oxide Patina (Heat Tarnish)
verdigrisStates.visualDescription: Uniform dark chocolate brown or penny-bronze dry film from regular cooking heat
verdigrisStates.toxicityHazard: Low-Moderate (Benign for neutral foods; dissolves in acidic sauces)

verdigrisStates.name: Black Cupric Oxide Scale (Gas Flame Overheating)
verdigrisStates.visualDescription: Flaky or dull matte black crust resulting from high-heat exposure to atmospheric oxygen
verdigrisStates.solubilityInAcid: High (Readily soluble in dilute food acids)
verdigrisStates.toxicityHazard: Moderate (Dissolves readily in boiling acidic liquids, releasing Cu2+)

verdigrisStates.name: Basic Copper Carbonate Verdigris (Atmospheric Moisture & CO2)
verdigrisStates.visualDescription: Pale mint-green to powdery turquoise chalky crust commonly found around rivets, rim, and damp storage spots
verdigrisStates.solubilityInAcid: Very High (Effervesces and dissolves instantly in acidic liquids)
verdigrisStates.toxicityHazard: Severe (Highly bioavailable copper salts that leach instantaneously into food)

verdigrisStates.name: Basic Copper Acetate Verdigris (Vinegar / Acid Residue Corrosion)
verdigrisStates.visualDescription: Intense dark emerald to sapphire blue-green crystalline crust formed by acid spills or unwashed vinegar residues
verdigrisStates.solubilityInAcid: Extreme (Completely water-soluble and instant gastric poison)
verdigrisStates.toxicityHazard: Extreme / Acute Danger (Consuming this salt induces violent vomiting and gastroenteritis)

retinningQuarterRule.rationale: When the aggregate area of bare copper exposed through a worn tin lining exceeds the surface area of a US quarter, galvanic corrosion and direct acidic contact leach toxic concentrations of copper into food, mandating immediate professional hand-wiped retinning.
